addresses.name: CCapitalTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`capital = <province id>`: is the scope country's declared capital that province.** 0x5F1C50 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5F1C83, 18 instructions, 12 int3 before.

    country = g_CCountryDataBase (0x1A855A4) ->+0x16C [scope->country_id (+0x14)]
    return country->capital_province_id (+0xE20) == this->value (+0x40)      ; sete

**Equality, not `>=`**, and the **declared** capital at +0xE20, not the acting capital at +0xE24 that `capital_scope` and the goods triggers use - so a country whose capital has fallen still answers its old capital here. `CIntTrigger` operand, raw `atoi`. `capital = this` / `= from` set the flags and zero the value, and nothing reads the flags, so they test `capital == 0`. No guard on the scope: a province-only scope carries country `---`/0, so the test reads the placeholder country 0 rather than failing.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry (VA 0x15F8E2C, slot 6). `mov edx,[eax+0xe20]; cmp edx,[ecx+0x40]; sete al`. +0xE20 is already capital_province_id in project.json and in bicelib_findings. Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a second reader path to +0xE24 inside the body - there is none, the body has no branch.

addresses.name: CFactionProgressTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`faction_progress = N`: does the scope country's faction hold at least N per cent of the world's victory points.** 0x5FD370 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5FD3B5, 26 instructions, 10 int3 before.

    country = g_CCountryDataBase (0x1A855A4) ->+0x16C [scope->country_id (+0x14)]
    CFaction::GetVictoryPointShare(country->faction (+0xD8), &share)   ; 0x122CC0
    return share >= this->value (+0x40)

`GetVictoryPointShare` answers `faction->Progress (+0xAC) * 1000 / (sum of every province's +0x34 * 1000)`, then `* 100000 / 1000` - a **percentage in thousandths** - and the operand is `CValueTrigger` thousandths, so `faction_progress = 50` is 50 per cent and decimals survive. **There is no divide on the operand**: the body has no `0x10624DD3`, which corrects FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3. `faction` is never null (a country in no faction points at the shared null faction), so no guard is needed. A dead store puts `scope->country_tag (+0x10)` in the slot that then receives the share. No guard on the scope: a province-only scope carries country `---`/0, so the test reads the placeholder country 0 rather than failing.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry; no 0x10624DD3 anywhere between 0x5FD370 and the ret. GetVictoryPointShare re-read to its `ret 8` at rva 0x122DF6: the sum loop multiplies +0x34 by 0x3E8, then 0xB99AF0/0xB99980 with 1000 and with 0x186A0 (100000) and 1000 - agreeing with its existing record. Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a savegame or live read where a faction with half the world's VP fails `faction_progress = 50`.

addresses.name: CIsThreatendTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`is_threatend = N`: does any neighbour pose the scope country a threat of at least N.** 0x5FAFB0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5FB018 (false) and 0x5FB022 (true), one frame, 9 int3 before.

    country = g_CCountryDataBase (0x1A855A4) ->+0x16C [scope->country_id (+0x14)]
    for (node = country->Neighbours (+0xFD8); node; node = node->+0xC)
        if (country->diplomacy_status_array (+0xE28) [node->+4 /* id */] ->threat (+0x5C) >= this->value (+0x40))
            return true
    return false

So it is the threat **the scope country feels** from each country on its `Neighbours` list - not from every country, and not the threat it poses. Both sides are thousandths (`CValueTrigger`, and `threat` is thousandths), so `is_threatend = 50` is 50 threat. An empty neighbour list is false. No guard on the scope: a province-only scope carries country `---`/0, so the test reads the placeholder country 0 rather than failing.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry: `mov eax,[eax+0xfd8]; test; je false`, loop body `mov ecx,[ecx+4]; mov ecx,[edx+ecx*4]; cmp [ecx+0x5c],edi; jge true`, `mov eax,[eax+0xc]` for the next node. +0xFD8 (Neighbours), +0xE28 (diplomacy_status_array) and CDiplomacyStatus +0x5C (threat) were all already in the record. Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: CCountryList's node keeping its next pointer anywhere but +0xC.

addresses.name: CMonthTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`month = M`: is the current month M or later in the year, counting January as 0.** 0x5D2B30 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D2C32, 15 int3 before. The scope is not read.

    days  = (state->tick (+0xBDC) - 43800000) / 24
    year  = (int)(days / 365.0)                                    ; double, 0x160A550
    doy   = days - (int)(float)((float)year * 365.0)
    m = 0; doy -= MonthLengthTable[0]                              ; 0x1713294
    while (doy >= 0) { m++; doy -= MonthLengthTable[m]; }
    return m >= this->value (+0x40)

**Zero-based** (1 January gives m = 0) and **`>=`**, so `month = 5` is June through December and `month = 0` is always true. Combined with `year`, `year = 1940 month = 5` is true from June to December 1940 and **false again in January 1941**. The date arithmetic is inlined, the same as RunHourlyTick's; it shares no helper with `CDateTrigger`, and unlike `date` it ignores `scope->days_in_month`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry; the loop is `sub eax,[0x1713294]; js; inc esi; sub eax,[esi*4+0x1713294]; jns`, then `cmp esi,[edi+0x40]; setge`. Walked by hand for day-of-year 0 (m = 0) and 31 (m = 1). Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a script `month = 1` firing in January in the running game.

addresses.name: CNationalismTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`nationalism = N`: is the scope province's nationalism strictly above N.** 0x5E6F70 to two `ret 4` at 0x5E7039 (true) and 0x5E704D (false), one frame, 15 int3 before.

    if (scope->province (+0x28) == 0) return false
    province = g_CCurrentGameState->+0xB8C [scope->province]
    return province->nationalism (+0x24) > this->value (+0x40) * 1000

**Strictly greater** (`jle` to false), unlike nearly every other leaf. `CIntTrigger` operand multiplied by 1000, so it cannot carry decimals: `nationalism = 2.5` is 2. A country-only scope is **false**, guarded.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry: `cmp [eax+0x28],ebx; je false` first, then `imul eax,eax,0x3e8; cmp [edx+0x24],eax; jle false`. CMapProvince +0x24 was already `nationalism`. Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: nothing short of a misdecode; the compare and its direction are one instruction each.

addresses.name: CNumOfCitiesTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`num_of_cities = N | this | from`: does the scope country own at least that many provinces.** 0x5D7F50 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5D7FDD, 7 int3 before. One of the two leaves that honour `this`/`from`.

    threshold = this->value (+0x40)
    if (this->arg_is_this (+0x18))      threshold = countries[EventScope_GetCountryTag(scope).id]->owned_province_count (+0xCF8)
    else if (this->arg_is_from (+0x19)) threshold = countries[scope->from_country_id (+0x1C)]->owned_province_count
    return countries[scope->country_id]->owned_province_count (+0xCF8) >= threshold

So 'cities' are **owned provinces**, every one of them. `this` goes through EventScope_GetCountryTag (falls back on a province's owner), `from` reads the scope's from_country directly; `this` is tested first. No guard on the scope: a province-only scope carries country `---`/0, so the test reads the placeholder country 0 rather than failing.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry; `cmp byte [ecx+0x18],0`, `call 0x9C1A40` (VA; rva 0x5C1A40) with the scope pushed and EDI = out (EventScope_GetCountryTag's recorded convention), `cmp byte [ecx+0x19],0`, then three reads of +0xCF8. +0xCF8 is already owned_province_count, and CNumOfRevoltsFractionTrigger divides by the same field. Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0xCF8 counting something narrower than owned provinces.

The game state's list of every ship sunk, by the ship's own owner tag. Operand thousandths truncated toward zero. A dead store of `owner (+0x94)` into a local each pass. addresses.name: CTotalSunkByUsTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`total_sunk_by_us = N`: how many ships on the sunk list were sunk by something of the scope country's that still exists.** 0x5FDE50 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5FDF85, 15 int3 before.

    n = 0
    for (node = g_CCurrentGameState->sunk_ships (+0x20); node; node = node->+8)
        ship = node->+0
        if (FindPersistentByIdPair(ship->sunk_by_type (+0x9C), ship->sunk_by_id (+0xA0))       ; 0x69D390
            && FindPersistentByIdPair(...)->+0x98 == scope->country_id) n++                    ; resolved twice
    return n >= this->value (+0x40) / 1000

The sinker is resolved from its saved id pair, and its **current** owner id at +0x98 - the CSubUnit owner slot, so the sinker is a sub unit (a ship or a wing; CSubUnit::SetSunkBy writes the pair). **A ship whose sinker no longer resolves is not counted**, so the figure can fall as the sinkers are lost - whether a sunk ship stays registered was not read. Operand thousandths truncated toward zero.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry: two `call 0xA9D390` (VA; rva 0x69D390) with the +0x9C/+0xA0 pair pushed by value, `test eax,eax; je skip` after the first, `cmp [eax+0x98],[ebx+0x14]` after the second. CSubUnit has CReferenceObject at offset 0, so no -8 adjustment is needed and none is made. Slot 6 of the class's only table and of no other (holders = 1), so the vftable fixes the entry (trap 2). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the sunk_by pair naming a CUnit (CPersistent at +8) - then +0x98 would be a CUnit field and the test would compare garbage.

addresses.name: CGovernmentPositionTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`<position> = <minister id>` (`head_of_state = 23050`): does the scope country's minister in that post have that id.** 0x5F59E0 to two `ret 4` at 0x5F5A4B (true) and 0x5F5A54 (false), one frame, 7 int3 before. The decompiler garbles it because FindPersistentById takes its key in EAX and its table in ECX.

    if (!g_PersistentIdTable_LowTypes [0x1A857F4]) return false
    m = FindPersistentById({type 0x26, id this->value (+0x40)})          ; 0x69DA00, EAX = &key
    if (!m) return false                                                   ; no such minister
    holder = countries[scope->country_id]->ministers (+0x618) [this->position (+0x44)->index (+0x4C)]
    return holder->id (+0xC) == m->id (+0xC)

Since `m` was found by that id, the comparison is `holder->id == value` with **an existence check in front**: an id no minister has is false even before the post is looked at. Type 0x26 is the minister registry - `minister_alive` looks up the same type and reads CMinister's start and death dates. The post's holder is dereferenced unguarded; whether an empty post holds a null pointer or a null minister was not read. Built only by Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey's first arm, with the operand `atoi`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the vftable entry (listing, not the decompile): `mov ecx,[0x1a857f4]; mov [esp+8],0x26; mov [esp+0xc],eax(+0x40); test ecx; je false; lea eax,[esp+8]; call 0xA9DA00; test eax; je false`, then `mov ecx,[ecx+0x618]; mov edx,[edx+0x4c]; mov edx,[ecx+edx*4]; mov ecx,[edx+0xc]; cmp ecx,[eax+0xc]`. addresses.name: CSubUnitTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`<unit type> = N` (`infantry_brigade = 4`), and as built it can only be true for N <= 0.** 0x5DABE0 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5DAC99, 4 int3 before.

    threshold = this->value (+0x40)
    if (this->arg_is_this (+0x18) || this->arg_is_from (+0x19))           ; unreachable from script
        other = arg_is_this ? EventScope_GetCountryTag(scope) : scope->from_country (+0x18/+0x1C)
        threshold = *CUnitList::SumSubUnitsOfDefinition(&countries[other.id]->units, def, &t) / 1000
    CUnitList::SumSubUnitsOfDefinition(&countries[scope->country_id]->units (+0xBAC), this->definition (+0x44), &n)   ; 0x1D62B0
    return n >= threshold * 1000

The sum compares each sub unit's `sub_unit_definition_ptr (+0x58)` **by pointer** with the trigger's definition, which Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey takes from `CSubUnitDataBase +0x10` - the database's template. But **every sub unit owns its own definition**: CSubUnit::CSubUnit allocates 0x228 bytes, constructs a CSubUnitDefinition and stores it at +0x58 (rva 0x1A8A6D), CSubUnit::SetType copies the template into it, and CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies rewrites it per sub unit. So the pointers never match, the sum is 0, and the test is `0 >= N*1000`. (`total_amount_of_brigades` compares `type_index` instead, which is how the game's own code tells types apart.) Had it matched, the figure would have been thousandths: 1000 per ship, and the remaining `strength (+0x5C)` of each brigade or wing - not a count.

**THIS/FROM**: the only constructor call is Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey's arm (0x5CFFEC), which hands slot 7 a token whose class is forced to 0xF; CIntTrigger's slot 7 sets the flags only for class 0x377/0x34F. So the branch is dead from script.
addresses.evidence: Listing read end to end. +0x58 per sub unit: CSubUnit::CSubUnit's `push 0x228; call operator_new` (rva 0x1A89FC), `call` rva 0x1A3510, `mov [esi+0x58],eax` (rva 0x1A8A6D); CSubUnit::SetType at rva 0x1ABF39 loads [edi+0x58] and copies the template into it through CSubUnitDefinition::Assign (rva 0x1A7500). Trigger side: rva 0x5CFFBA `call CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance; add eax,0x10; call StringHashFind` gives the definition handed to CSubUnitTrigger's ctor (0x5C8B30, which stores it at +0x44); findRefs finds one call to that ctor. 0x5D1400 tests `cmp eax,0x377` / `0x34f` on the token class the loader sets to 0xF at 0x5CFF8C. Confidence is on the reading; the 'always false' conclusion is inferred (likely). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: any writer that stores a database definition into CSubUnit +0x58, or `infantry_brigade = 1` evaluating true in a running game - a BiceLib probe settles it in one call.

addresses.name: CLastBattleWinnerLossesTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**`last_battle_winner_losses = N`: were the winner's losses in the last land battle strictly more than N.** 0x602200 to the single `ret 4` at 0x6022A5, 4 int3 before.

addresses.name: CUnitList::SumSubUnitsOfDefinition
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CUnitList::SumSubUnitsOfDefinition(CUnitList* units@ECX, CSubUnitDefinition* definition@EDI, int* out@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.evidence: Read to its ret: `mov dword [eax],0` first; `call [vft+0x40]` (CUnit slot 16 IsNaval); naval arm `cmp [edx+0x58],edi; jne; inc ecx`, then `imul ecx,ecx,0x3e8; add [eax],ecx`; other arm `add edx,[ecx+0x5c]`. findRefs --callers 0x5D62B0 gives exactly the three sites. Not Lua-registered (luabind.json has the three neighbouring counters and not this one). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a fourth caller outside the trigger, through a pointer.

addresses.name: FindPersistentByIdPair
addresses.comment: **The by-value front end of FindPersistentById.** 0x69D390 to two bare `ret`s at 0x69D3BA and 0x69D3C0, 15 int3 after. Takes the `{type, id}` pair as two stack dwords, picks the registry `[0x1A857F0]` when `type > 0x1268` and `[0x1A857F4]` otherwise, answers 0 when that registry does not exist, and otherwise calls FindPersistentById (0x69DA00) with EAX = the address of its own argument pair. The pointer is the registered object as stored - for a CUnit that is its CReferenceObject at +8, which is why callers holding a unit's id add -8 and callers holding a sub unit's do not. 106 direct call sites. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: `cmp dword [ebp+8],0x1268; mov ecx,[0x1a857f0]; ja; mov ecx,[0x1a857f4]; test ecx,ecx; je zero; lea eax,[ebp+8]; call 0xa9da00`, bare `ret` on both exits, and the callers in CTotalSunkByUsTrigger::Evaluate push the pair with `sub esp,8` and pop it with `add esp,8` - cdecl. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a caller that does not clean the eight bytes.

addresses.name: CBuildingTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment:
**The one body in the family that divides the *field* by 1000 instead of scaling the operand**, which is why a scan for the divide-by-1000 magic must look at the instruction and not just at the class's base. 0x5DC040 to the single `ret 4` at 0x5DC112, 69 instructions, seven int3 before and eleven after.

    state    = g_CCurrentGameState[0x1A89790]                       ; the lazy accessor, inlined
    province = state->+0xB8C[ scope->province (+0x28) ]
    level    = province->+0x310[ this->building (+0x44)->+0x54 ]->level_max (+0x20)
    return level / 1000 >= this->value (+0x40)

The operand is a plain integer (`CIntTrigger`, `atoi`) and the stored level is thousandths, so `<building_name> = 3` means level 3. Like `CTechnologyTrigger` it keeps the thing it names in a pointer at +0x44, resolved at load time.

**It reads the built level, not the working one**: CProvinceBuilding +0x20 is `level_max`, what was built; `level_current` (+0x24), what bombing has left of it, is not read. So a bombed-out factory still answers its full level here. The divide truncates toward zero. **Unguarded**: a country-only scope reads province 0, the placeholder.

Its keyword is **not** in `CTrigger::LoadKey`'s 152-case table (`findings/FINDINGS-script.md`'s trigger list has `has_building` for `CHasBuildingTrigger` and nothing for this class), so it is reached through the loader's default arm - which is consistent with the key being a building's own name.
addresses.evidence: REVISED: comment only - adds that +0x20 is level_max (built) and not level_current (+0x24), plus the province-0 note; everything else is the existing text. Bytes: `imul dword ptr [edx+0x20]` at 0x5DC0F3 with edx the CProvinceBuilding; CProvinceBuilding +0x20 level_max / +0x24 level_current are already in project.json and bicelib_findings (Max / Current). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the two fields being the other way round - CProvinceBuilding +0x28 `changed`'s comment (bombing moves the current level) agrees with this assignment.

struct_fields.name: last_battle_winner_losses
struct_fields.comment: The last land battle's winner losses, for the whole world - one figure, overwritten by CCombat::Conclude (0x174580) each time a battle of that kind ends, anywhere. Read only by the `last_battle_winner_losses` trigger. A plain number: the side's CCombatant losses (+0x84) / 1000, plus a term for the side's remaining units when the side's unnamed byte +0xA8 is set (land: total strength x 100; naval: ships; air: wings - read in the decompile, not the listing). Not in the savegame's top level.
struct_fields.evidence: Writer: CCombat::Conclude stores the six at 0x174879 (+0x34), 0x17491C (+0x30), 0x174A21 (+0x44), 0x174AC4 (+0x40), 0x174BC9 (+0x3C), 0x174C6C (+0x38), in the branches for combat kind 1, 2 and 3, the loser's figure chosen on `attackerLost`. Readers: the six CLast*Trigger::Evaluate bodies, whose class names give the same winner/loser and land/air/naval assignment independently. A scan of every singleton-held access to +0x30..+0x44 finds those six reads and no other coherent writer (the other candidates' registers had been reloaded - checked one by one). WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a writer reached through a register the scan does not track.
